clue.text: River's sudden race

definitions.meaning: a river in Devon, in south-west England
a quick sudden dash or rush forward

explanation.surface: A river described as rushing suddenly downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a Devon river, and a dart is a quick sudden movement or dash.

clue.text: Unruly brutes need the stocks!

indicators.note: unruly things are disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A cry that wild louts deserve to be pilloried in the old public stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges BRUTES and NEED together. 'the stocks' sounds like the wooden frame for punishment, but means financial securities.
explanation.definitionFit: Debentures are bonds or loan securities, a kind of financial stock.

clue.text: A sovereign measure?

definitions.meaning: a monarch who reigns over a country
a straight strip marked in inches or centimetres for measuring

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch rules a kingdom, and the same word names a straight measuring stick.

clue.text: Man put on a lot of weight — energetic dancing's the answer

indicators.note: one piece is placed on after another, so the second follows the first

parts.note: Charles is a man's name
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A man has gained weight, and lively dancing is offered as the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance with fast kicking steps.

clue.text: The chap's conservative record of past times

parts.note: belonging to the chap, i.e. his
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A man's right-wing record of bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: History is the chronicle of events from former times.

clue.text: Car tore around the nuclear plant

indicators.note: the letters are turned about and placed in a new order here

explanation.surface: A car speeds round and round a nuclear power station.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the apparatus in which a controlled nuclear chain reaction takes place.

clue.text: Muse on an age approaching

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so it comes first

parts.note: an era is an age or epoch
to as in 'to the house', heading towards

explanation.surface: A goddess of inspiration reflects on an era that is drawing near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb, ponder, but is one of the nine Greek goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek myth.

clue.text: Treasure Island character giving no quarter to ten lawyers in dispute

indicators.note: lawyers in dispute are at odds, so the letters are jumbled
giving up the named letter means it is removed

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A character from a classic novel refuses to show mercy to a group of quarrelling lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving no' removes S, a compass quarter, from LAWYERS to leave LAWYER; 'in dispute' then rearranges TEN with LAWYER.
explanation.definitionFit: Squire Trelawney is the landowner who funds the voyage in Stevenson's novel of buried gold.

clue.text: Money you don't miss?

definitions.meaning: a piece of paper currency, a banknote
to observe or mark something, so it is not overlooked

explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is paper money, and to note something is to notice it rather than let it slip past.

clue.text: First lady ill — beer-swilling — he writes maliciously

indicators.note: the first letter of the word lady is taken
swilling sloshes liquid about, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: A leading woman, unwell, has been knocking back beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but just gives L; 'swilling' rearranges ILL and BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who publishes false, damaging written statements about another person commits libel.

clue.text: It's a cable adrift, off Sweden

indicators.note: something adrift has come loose and wanders, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A ship's cable has come loose and is floating near the Swedish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location phrase: the body of water lying off Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea lies along Sweden's eastern coast, between Scandinavia and the Baltic states.

clue.text: A fellow advocate

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man who speaks up on someone's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts for someone else, as a representative or spokesman does.

clue.text: Language offering a choice of directions

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction
or offers a choice between two things
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A tongue that lets you pick which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a choice of directions' supplies all three pieces: two compass points with the word of choice between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the medieval tongue of Scandinavia and the Vikings.

clue.text: May be changed into opal, if you wish

indicators.note: letters that can be changed can be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A gem can be altered, should you like it to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be changed' rearranges INTO and OPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left to choice, done only at your wish, is not compulsory.

clue.text: Tormented: base wickedness encouraged it

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as a bed of concrete
evil is wickedness
led as in guided or drew someone on

explanation.surface: Someone driven to torment by underlying sin that was egged on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedevilled means plagued or harassed, as if by demons.

clue.text: American friend going round the bend as a matter of course

indicators.note: these pieces circle the next one, which sits inside them

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for American
an ally is a friend
U for a U-bend or U-turn shape

explanation.surface: An American pal is driven mad, as tends to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round the bend' reads as the idiom for going mad; here the bend is the U shape, and 'going round' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done normally or habitually happens in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Slip, perhaps, below the surface of the river

parts.note: under means beneath
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: Someone slipping and going beneath the water of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' reads as a stumble but is a woman's undergarment, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is an example of a garment worn beneath outer clothes.

clue.text: For example, under no circumstances return to exact it?

definitions.note: the thing one sets out to inflict or exact on a wrongdoer

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: never means not in any situation

explanation.surface: A warning never, ever to come back and take your due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses EG followed by NEVER as one string. The definition leans on the phrase 'exact revenge', so the question mark flags an indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution is something you exact from a person who has wronged you.

clue.text: Out to get even — even Gulf war

indicators.note: war brings destruction and disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Gulf conflict fought to settle scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set on retaliation, wanting to pay back a wrong, is vindictive.

clue.text: Advocate, Irish-speaking, holds don in error

indicators.note: the first piece grips the second, which goes inside it

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

indicators.note: something in error is wrong, so the letters are put wrongly

explanation.surface: An Irish-speaking supporter keeps a university lecturer in a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a university lecturer but is only fodder; 'in error' scrambles it before 'holds' places it inside the Irish language.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a view is to support or approve it publicly.

clue.text: Girl, English and alone, going out on the river

indicators.note: letters going out break from their order and are rearranged

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An English girl by herself heads out onto the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges ALONE, set between E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Painter of waggon beside the ditch

indicators.note: the pieces sit next to each other in this order

parts.note: a van is a covered waggon or wagon
a dyke is a ditch or drainage channel

explanation.surface: An artist depicting a cart parked next to a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter of' sounds like an artist's subject, but 'of' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony van Dyck, often spelt Vandyke in English, was a Flemish portrait artist.

clue.text: I am able to support tax for this city

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
I can means I am able

explanation.surface: Someone offers to bear the tax burden for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is the tiny papal state inside Rome.

clue.text: Small amount of grant for me — or not?

indicators.note: the letters of the word or are taken away and the rest are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of a grant is offered to me, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: GRANT FOR ME holds the answer's letters plus OR; 'or not' removes OR and the question mark invites the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece or bit broken off something larger.

clue.text: Infer it's not a right angle

indicators.note: an angle that is not right is out of true, so its letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A geometry remark that an angle is not ninety degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a right' signals the rearranging of ANGLE, not a deletion of R.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather or deduce information bit by bit.

clue.text: One result of a successful bore

definitions.text: One result of a successful bore

parts.words: One result of a successful bore
parts.note: a drill bore may succeed in striking oil, but a tedious person who succeeds leaves listeners weary

explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weariness and boredom, what a tedious person induces.

clue.text: Stuff from Northern Ireland? No, from France

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: Is this material from Northern Ireland? No, it comes from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon.

clue.text: Many a round of applause

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a lap is one circuit or round of a track

explanation.surface: Lots of people give a burst of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A clap is a slap of the hands together in approval.

clue.text: An old master in Belgium

definitions.meaning: a feudal lord to whom service was owed
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord was a feudal superior, and Liège is a Belgian city.

clue.text: Wild cat on run — large not active by day

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feral cat on the loose, a big one that only comes out at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles three words of the clue together; the abbreviation for large is added after the scrambled part.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that sleep through daylight and are active after dark behave this way.

clue.text: Gin rejected — no good in Ireland, as the poet said, for coupling

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A rejected drink, worthless in Ireland in poetic words, for a pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink but is an animal snare; 'rejected' reads it backwards. 'as the poet said' marks the old poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Partnering is pairing up with someone, a kind of joining together.

clue.text: In conclusion I get the girl

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the word for conclusion

parts.note: the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: At last the hero wins the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's given name.
